question:
Equilateral \(\triangle ABC\) with side length \(14\) is rotated about its center by angle \(\theta,\) where \(0 \lt \theta \lt 60^\circ,\) to form \(\triangle DEF.\) See the figure. The area of hexagon \(ADBECF\) is \(91\sqrt3.\) What is \(\tan\theta?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_12B_Q19_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The rotation preserves threefold symmetry, so the hexagon's area lets us find the height of one added triangle. Let \(O\) be the common center, and write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). A \(120^\circ\) rotation about \(O\) carries \(ADB\) to \(BEC\) and then to \(CFA\), so these triangles are congruent. Together with \(ABC\), they partition the hexagon with disjoint interiors.

The altitude of \(ABC\) is \(\sqrt{14^2-7^2}=7\sqrt3\), so
\[
[ABC]=49\sqrt3,
\qquad
[ADB]=\frac{91\sqrt3-49\sqrt3}{3}=14\sqrt3.
\]
Since \(AB=14\), the perpendicular distance from \(D\) to \(AB\) is \(2\sqrt3\).

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). Equilateral-triangle symmetry gives \(OM\perp AB\), \(\angle OAM=30^\circ\), and \(\angle AOM=60^\circ\). The resulting \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle gives
\[
OM=\frac7{\sqrt3},
\qquad OA=OD=\frac{14}{\sqrt3}.
\]
In the orientation shown, \(A\) rotates toward ray \(OM\). Thus \(0<\theta<60^\circ\) puts \(D\) inside \(\angle AOM\), across \(AB\) from \(O\).

Draw through \(D\) a line parallel to \(AB\). Let it meet ray \(OM\) at \(N\) and ray \(OA\) at \(K\). Here \(N\) is beyond \(M\), and \(D\) lies between \(K\) and \(N\). Therefore
\[
ON=\frac7{\sqrt3}+2\sqrt3=\frac{13}{\sqrt3}.
\]
Right triangle \(ODN\) now gives
\[
DN=\sqrt{OD^2-ON^2}
=\sqrt{\frac{196-169}{3}}=3.
\]
Triangle \(ONK\) also has angles \(30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ\), so \(KN=\sqrt3\,ON=13\). Consequently, \(KD=13-3=10\).

Finally, drop the perpendicular \(DH\) to \(OA\). Since \(\theta\) is acute, \(H\) lies on ray \(OA\). Also, \(\angle DKH=30^\circ\), so the side opposite this angle is half the hypotenuse:
\[
DH=\frac{KD}{2}=5.
\]
Using right triangle \(ODH\),
\[
OH=\sqrt{\frac{196}{3}-25}=\frac{11}{\sqrt3}.
\]
Because \(\angle DOH=\theta\), we obtain
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{DH}{OH}
=\frac5{11/\sqrt3}
=\boxed{\frac{5\sqrt3}{11}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
